key_insight: The models agreed strongly on lung cancer predictions, but their explanations were often inconsistent, showing that similar outputs can come from very different reasoning.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI, high accuracy alone is not enough; interpretability should be checked separately to help ensure models rely on relevant lung regions.
method: Compared three models: a CNN, pretrained ResNet50, and ViT
Used the IQ-OTH/NCCD lung CT dataset for training and evaluation
Applied LIME plus a dual-correlation framework to assess prediction agreement and explanation agreement
evidence_signal: ResNet50, CNN, and ViT reached 98.61%, 97.91%, and 93.75% accuracy respectively, with ROC-AUC 0.99 for all, while prediction correlations were >0.99 but LIME explanation correlations stayed below 0.26.
watch_item: Very high prediction agreement may hide unreliable reasoning, so explanation methods like LIME should be validated before using such models in clinical settings.
paper_title: Trusting Right Predictions for Wrong Reasons: A LIME Based Analysis of Deep Learning Interpretability in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
